title: What the agile mindset is
blurb: Describe the agile mindset as PRINCE2 Agile defines it and recognize how it shapes responses to change, value and collaboration.
question: Which statement best describes the agile mindset according to PRINCE2 Agile?

teach.h: The mindset is a way of thinking
teach.body: PRINCE2 Agile describes the agile mindset as a way of thinking and approaching work that fosters adaptability and encourages continual learning, improvement and flexibility. It is not a tool, a process or a certificate. In plain English: someone with an agile mindset expects things to change, looks for what they can learn from each result, and keeps improving how they work rather than defending how it was done before.

teach.h: Why the mindset is the core of agility
teach.body: The book says agile's true value lies in shifting mindsets, supported by a culture that empowers teams to self-manage, decide and innovate. Frameworks, processes and practices give structure, but they do not guarantee agility on their own. That is why the mindset sits at the centre of the Agile Onion: it is the way of thinking that drives everything around it.

teach.h: How the mindset shapes three everyday attitudes
head: Faced with
Agile mindset
Fixed habit
rows: A chance to learn and adapt
Focus effort on what users need

teach.h: Growth mindset: often seen as the heart of it
teach.body: PRINCE2 Agile describes the growth mindset as the fundamental belief that any person can learn, adapt to change and therefore grow. The book notes that it is often seen as the core of the agile mindset itself. A team that believes skills can be developed will try new ways of working, ask for feedback and treat setbacks as learning, which is exactly the adaptability the agile mindset needs.

The mindset links to the agile values and principles around it. Agile values shift the focus from rigid processes to people, collaboration and user value. Agile principles include welcoming changing requirements, even late in development. A team with an agile mindset therefore asks 'does this change add value for users?' rather than 'is this change in the plan?', and works with users and colleagues to find the answer.

root.label: Users ask for a change late on

children.label: Refuse: it is not in the plan
Check its value, learn, adapt priorities

teach.body: Halden Bay Water is replacing its customer billing portal. In iteration 4, a pilot group says the new payment page confuses older customers. Team coach Priya Raman hears two reactions: one developer wants to defend the design because it matches the specification; another suggests testing a simpler version next iteration. The team chooses the test, learns from the result and improves the page. That choice, learning and adapting rather than defending the plan, is the agile mindset at work.

teach.text: The agile mindset is not something an organization gets by adopting Scrum, Kanban or a new tool. Those are processes and practices. The mindset is a way of thinking that fosters adaptability and continual learning, and the book treats it as where agile's real value lies.

items: Agile mindset: a way of thinking and approaching work that fosters adaptability.
It encourages continual learning, improvement and flexibility.
Growth mindset (anyone can learn, adapt and grow) is often seen as its core.
Agile's true value lies in shifting mindsets, not in adopting a framework.
The mindset treats change as a chance to learn and focuses effort on user value.

summary: You can now describe the agile mindset as a way of thinking that fosters adaptability and encourages continual learning, improvement and flexibility. You can also explain why the growth mindset is often seen as its core and how the mindset shapes responses to change, value and collaboration.

A.q: Which statement best describes the agile mindset according to PRINCE2 Agile?
options: A set of events that every agile team must hold
A way of thinking that fosters adaptability and learning
A framework for planning work in short iterations
A checklist of techniques for prioritizing the team's work
A.why: The agile mindset is a way of thinking and approaching work that fosters adaptability and encourages continual learning, improvement and flexibility (2.6.1).

whyNot.0: Events are practices, an outer layer of the Agile Onion, not the mindset.
whyNot.2: A framework for iterative planning is a process, not a way of thinking.
whyNot.3: Techniques such as prioritization are practices, not the mindset.

A.q: Which concept does PRINCE2 Agile say is often seen as the core of the agile mindset itself?
A.why: The growth mindset, the belief that any person can learn, adapt and grow, is often seen as the core of the agile mindset (2.7.3).

whyNot.0: Servant leadership is a leadership style that supports agile maturity, not the core of the mindset.
whyNot.1: Rich communication supports agile maturity but is not described as the core of the mindset.
whyNot.3: Training and coaching help people understand change; they are not the core of the mindset.

A.q: Identify the missing word in the following sentence. The agile mindset encourages continual learning, improvement and [?].
A.why: The book describes the agile mindset as encouraging continual learning, improvement and flexibility (2.6.1).

whyNot.0: Standardization favours fixed ways of working rather than adaptation.
whyNot.1: Predictability is a feature of plan-driven thinking, not the agile mindset.
whyNot.2: Compliance with rules is not what the agile mindset is said to encourage.

B.q: A department head says, 'Anyone on this team can learn the new ways of working if we support them.' Which concept from PRINCE2 Agile does this reflect?
B.why: The growth mindset is the belief that any person can learn, adapt to change and grow (2.6.1, 2.7.3).

whyNot.1: Servant leadership is about the leader serving the team's needs, not a belief that people can grow.
whyNot.2: Rich communication is about conveying words, emotions, visuals and body language.
whyNot.3: Being versus doing agile contrasts mindset with mechanics; the statement is about the ability to grow.

B.q: Late in development, users ask for a change to a feature. Which response best reflects an agile mindset?
options: Reject it so the agreed plan is protected
Assess its value and adapt priorities
Defer all changes until the final release
Add it at once without checking its value
B.why: The agile mindset fosters adaptability and focuses on user value; agile principles welcome changing requirements, even late in development (2.6.1).

whyNot.0: Protecting the plan over user value is the fixed thinking the mindset moves away from.
whyNot.2: Holding every change back removes the chance to learn and adapt during delivery.
whyNot.3: Adapting is not the same as accepting everything; the mindset looks at value to users.

B.q: According to PRINCE2 Agile, agile values shift the focus from rigid processes towards which of these?
B.why: The book says agile values shift the focus from rigid processes to people, collaboration and user value (2.6.1).

whyNot.0: Detailed plans and sign-off reflect a plan-driven focus, not agile values.
whyNot.1: Tools, frameworks and terminology are the doing side of agile.
whyNot.3: Contracts and documentation are what the Manifesto values less than collaboration and working products.

C.q:
Which two statements about the agile mindset are correct?
1. It fosters adaptability in how people approach work.
2. Adopting an agile framework guarantees it.
3. The growth mindset is often seen as its core.
4. It is mainly about following processes precisely.
C.why: The mindset fosters adaptability (1), and the growth mindset is often seen as its core (3) (2.6.1, 2.7.3).

whyNot.1: Statement 2 is wrong: the book says adopting a framework does not by itself guarantee agile benefits.
whyNot.2: Both are wrong: a framework guarantees nothing and precise process-following is not the mindset.
whyNot.3: Statement 4 is wrong: processes are an outer layer, not the mindset.

C.q: At Tolland Freight, an experiment with a new route-planning screen fails in testing. A manager wants to find out who was at fault. Which response reflects the agile mindset, and why?
options: Name the developer, because accountability builds trust
Stop experiments, because failure wastes the budget
Review what was learned, because the mindset values learning
Return to the old design, because the plan was agreed
C.why: The agile mindset encourages continual learning and improvement; a failed experiment is feedback to learn from (2.6.1).

whyNot.0: Blaming individuals discourages the learning and experimenting the mindset depends on.
whyNot.1: Stopping experiments removes the adaptability and learning the mindset fosters.
whyNot.3: Reverting because of the plan ignores the feedback the experiment produced.

C.q: An organization has introduced agile processes, but many staff believe their abilities are fixed and avoid trying new methods. What does PRINCE2 Agile suggest is lacking, and why does it matter?
options: A clearer framework, because processes create agility
Stricter roles, because structure builds confidence
More tools, because practices are the core
A growth mindset, because it is often seen as the core
C.why: The growth mindset, the belief that anyone can learn, adapt and grow, is often seen as the core of the agile mindset; processes alone do not guarantee agility (2.6.1, 2.7.3).

whyNot.0: Processes alone do not guarantee agility; the gap here is a belief about ability.
whyNot.1: Stricter roles do not change people's belief that they cannot grow.
whyNot.2: Practices are an outer layer and only scratch the surface of agility.

blocks.body: A machine runs the same programme whatever the weather. A gardener watches what grows, learns from each season and adjusts. The agile mindset is gardener thinking: adaptable, always learning and improving, flexible when conditions change. Underneath sits the growth mindset: the belief that people, like plants, can grow when supported.

blocks.text: If an option says the agile mindset is a framework, a set of events or a toolset, it has described an outer layer of the Agile Onion instead.

explain.body: The agile mindset is a way of thinking and approaching work that fosters adaptability and encourages continual learning, improvement and flexibility (2.6.1).

test.q: What does the agile mindset foster, according to PRINCE2 Agile?
test.why: The agile mindset is a way of thinking that fosters adaptability (2.6.1).

whyNot.1: Predictability is the aim of plan-driven approaches.
whyNot.2: Standardization favours fixed ways of working.
whyNot.3: Specialization in silos works against the collaboration agile values.

explain.body: The belief that any person can learn, adapt to change and grow. PRINCE2 Agile says it is often seen as the core of the agile mindset (2.6.1, 2.7.3).

test.q: Which describes the growth mindset in PRINCE2 Agile?
options: Leading a team by serving its needs
Believing any person can learn and grow
Training people and coaching them on the job
test.why: The growth mindset is the fundamental belief that any person can learn, adapt to change and grow (2.7.3).

whyNot.3: This is the training and coaching concept.

explain.body: Agile's true value lies in shifting mindsets, supported by a culture that lets teams self-manage, decide and innovate. Frameworks alone do not guarantee it (2.3).

test.q: According to PRINCE2 Agile, where does the true value of agile lie?
options: In detailed plans for every iteration
In tools that track team progress
test.why: The book says agile's true value lies in shifting mindsets (2.3).

whyNot.0: Adopting a framework does not by itself guarantee agile benefits.
whyNot.1: Detailed up-front plans are not where agile's value comes from.
whyNot.3: Tools support practices but do not create the mindset.

explain.body: Agile values move focus from rigid processes to people, collaboration and user value. Agile principles welcome changing requirements, even late on (2.6.1).

test.q: A team with an agile mindset is offered a change that would add clear value for users. What is its most likely reaction?
options: Refuse it because it was not planned
Wait for the next project to include it
Ask the board to rewrite the whole plan
Adapt its priorities to include it
test.why: The agile mindset fosters adaptability and focuses on user value, so the team adapts its priorities (2.6.1).

whyNot.0: Refusing valuable change because of the plan is fixed thinking.
whyNot.1: Delaying valuable change to a later project loses the value now.
whyNot.2: Adapting priorities does not require rewriting the whole plan.
